lawyer:
Rafique-ul Huq with Md Abdus Samad and Faheemul Huq, Advocates—For Petitioners of both the matters. 
Rokanuddin Mahmud with Sheikh Awsafur Rahman, Advocates—For Respondent Nos. 1 and 2 of Matter No. 60 of 2000 and for Respondent No. 1 of Matter No. 61 of 2000.
parties:
Akhtaruzzaman Chowdhury and anr ------- Petitioners
Vs
United Commercial Bank Ltd and others ------- Respondents
full_judgment: 10. Mr Rafique-ul Huq, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioners of Matter No. 60 of 2000, made a very brief submission in opposing the application for direction for summons. Mr Huq firstly, submitted that the well settled proposition of law is that rectification proceedings initiated under section 43 of the Act is a summary proceeding and there is no or little scope of taking any evidence in such proceedings. The learned Advocate then submits that they are the petitioners in this matter and onus is on them to establish their case. If they have not been able to bring the necessary materials on record they will feel the consequences and their application will fail and they will not get the reliefs prayed for. The learned Advocate further submits that in the instant case controversy veers round the fact whether the transfer of the shares, in fact, took place on 22-4-1996 as stated by the petitioners and if there are sufficient materials already on record from which this Court can arrive at a finding in one way or the other without taking any evidence at all. Therefore, the purpose of filing this application by the respondent No. 1 is nothing but an unholy attempt on their part to further delay the disposal of this proceeding and this factum is substantiated by the fact that the matter was filed as back as on 31-5-2000 and earlier this matter came up for hearing before two other Company judges in the past and the matters were heard in part in the past by two other Company Benches and it is only when before this Bench the parties have made full-fledged argument on the merits of the case, the respondent No. 1 has come up with this application which is nothing but a vexatious one and filed with the ulterior motive to further delay the disposal of the application so that the benefit derived by the petitioners by purchase of the shares is delayed for further uncertain period and also to deprive the petitioners of Matter No. 60 of 2000 from their legitimate claim. Mr Huq further submits that there is no law in our country which can compel a party to appear before a Court as a witness and in the instant case it is the petitioners who would be adversely affected if their application fails and they themselves do not feel it necessary at all to adduce any evidence inasmuch as they have put all the material facts and the documents through the affidavits and this Court is competent to dispose of the matter on the basis of the said materials. Mr Huq finally submitted that the respondent No. 1 bank relying on certain circumstances tried to impress upon this Court that the transaction that took place in between the respondent Nos. 2- 7 on the one hand and the petitioners of Matter No. 61 of 2000 on the other is fake or not a genuine one. Whether it is fake and genuine one can be decided on the basis of the materials placed by the respondent No. 1 bank in this matter as well as the materials filed by the petitioners of both the matters. Mr Huq submits that the controversy between the petitioners and the respondent bank is that although the shares were transferred on 22-4-96 but before 1999 the petitioners of Matter No. 61 of 2000 had never approached the bank for rectification of the share register on the basis of their purchase and it is also contended in the affidavit-in-opposition filed by the bank that when 'within the time-frame of one year the bank had written a letter on 20-5-96 drawing attention of the father and mother of the respondent Nos. 2-7 of Matter No. 61 of 2000 as to the provision of section 14Ka of the Bank Companies Act the parents of respondent Nos. 2-7 also did not disclose the fact of transfer of the shares to them. As against that the case of the respondent Nos. 2-7 is that no such letter was .ever received by their father and mother as alleged by the bank and although they have contended that they have written such a letter but no proof of such letter has been filed by the bank and they did not annex any postal receipt or acknowledgment due to show that any such communication was ever made with the petitioners of Matter No. 60 of 2000 and unless a person can show that a letter was sent to the correct address of the recipient no presumption can be drawn under section 27 of the General Clauses Act that the letter was received by the recipient. Therefore, Mr Huq emphatically submitted that there are sufficient materials on record to dispose of the application effectively and there is no necessity at all to examine or cross-examine any witness.
